newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco to privatise ONMT tourism body.
newsitem.headline: Morocco to privatise ONMT tourism body.

text.p: Morocco plans to privatise the state-owned Office National Marocain du Tourisme (ONMT) to improve its image abroad and attract more tourists, Les Nouvelles du Nord newspaper said on Friday.
The newspaper quoting the Tourism Minister Mohamed Alaoui M'Hamedi said: "The ONMT will be transformed into a private company with a capital held 50/50 by private and public sectors."
Alaoui gave no date for the privatisation.
ONMT has more than a dozen offices abroad, including in the United States and Japan.
Since the Gulf war in 1991, the number of foreign visitors to Morocco has declined from more than 4.0 million to around 3.0 million a year.
The ONMT is often described by opposition newspapers as "an overstaffed bureau with no efficient marketing strategy for Morocco's tourism products."

But a recent report issued by the Office des Changes said tourism receipts have improved in the first half of the year and rose 25.7 percent to 5.15 billion dirhams ($592 million), compared with the same time last year.
Under its privatisation programme, Morocco has already sold 45 state-owned companies, including hotels. It plans to privatise 70 other enterprises by end 1998.
The ONMT is not included in the present list of the firms to be privatised but Privatisation Minister Abderrahman Saadi said in remarks published last week that a new list was to be drawn up.
To speed up privatisation, he said his ministry was proposing reforms, particularly in the way the price of stock was being determined.
